accuracy_expectation: Expect about +/-0.5 mm over the full 36 x 48 in sheet after calibration (an estimate, not a measurement), against +/-0.2 mm for the recommended build.
summary: Same machine layout built from generic marketplace parts: V-slot extrusion with plastic V-wheels instead of linear rails, open-loop motors on a $30 controller, MDF bed with tape. Shipping included; shop-made brackets come from scrap and are not in the total.
tradeoffs: The CAD, Haas programs and printed parts are built around the rails and servo of the recommended build. The wheel plates, carriage and servo mount have to be redesigned and re-verified, and that time is not in the total.
Open-loop motors: a skipped step (snag, belt slip) is not detected, so a plot can go off without warning.
Plastic V-wheels on generic extrusion: no straightness figure, wheels need preload set by hand and wear over time.
No steel bed or magnets: paper is taped down, which is slower and can lift on large sheets.
risks: Redesign time: the existing CAD and the 16 Haas programs do not fit V-wheels, the MG90S or the DLC32 as they are. The new end plates, carriage and mounts are unpriced engineering and machining hours.

Accuracy is not proven. +/-0.5 mm is an estimate built on belt-stretch data for a generic 6 mm GT2 belt and an assumed 2-5 N rolling drag that has not been measured. Wheel preload drift, POM flat spots or a bent extrusion could push the error past that, and open-loop motors will not report lost steps.

Marketplace volatility: several lowest-price listings were nearly sold out on 2026-10-05 (MGN9 1 left, A4988 4 left, pulleys 4 left, motors 5 left). The DLC32 sale ends Oct 7 (regular $34.23) and the extrusion was a limited-time deal. Another seller's '2040 V-slot' listing has a review saying it arrived as T-slot, so check the profile on arrival.
The E-stop is rated 660 V 10 A, but the page gives no DC breaking rating, and it sits in the 24 V DC line.
Masking tape hold-down on blue bond can lift or tear a sheet, and the bed is not magnetic, so the recommended paper stops and magnet workflow does not apply.

The servo signal on the DLC32 laser header (gpio.32) comes from a community FluidNC config. Whether that header buffers or inverts the signal was not verified; check it on the bench before building the pen lift.

summary_full: The same flatbed gantry (two Y motors with auto-squaring, 36 x 48 in sheets, gravity pen with servo lift) built from generic marketplace parts: the 2040 V-slot frame doubles as the Y and X track for POM V-wheels, driven by open-loop NEMA17s on an MKS DLC32 running FluidNC. Gantry plates, brackets and pen tools are made in the shop from scrap aluminium and the 3D printer, which are not in the total; shipping is included (all lines ship free or are store pickup), sales tax is not.
tradeoffs_full: vs the recommended build: POM V-wheels on generic V-slot replace Hiwin MGN15 rails. The VEVOR listing gives no straightness figure, the wheels need eccentric preload set by hand and re-checked, and POM wears.

vs the recommended build: open-loop NEMA17s on A4988 drivers replace StepperOnline closed-loop kits. A skipped step (snag, crash, belt slip) is not detected or corrected, so a plot can go off without warning.

vs the recommended build: a generic 9 mm GT2 belt replaces Gates. Same width and pulley ratio (40 mm per turn), but the pitch and stiffness are not certified, so steps/mm must be calibrated on a long test plot.

vs the recommended build: MDF with masking tape replaces the steel-faced bed with 30 magnets. Drops $253.04 of steel sheet, magnets and contact cement for $5.58 of tape, but taping is slower and the tape can lift on large sheets.
vs the recommended build: MG90S replaces the Hitec HS-5065MG and its aluminium horn. Centering repeatability is not published, and the servo bracket and lift tab must be redrawn for the MG90S body.
vs the recommended build: MKS DLC32 replaces the FluidNC 6x. It has exactly 3 driver sockets, so there are no spare axes for a future automatic pen rack, and the servo uses the laser PWM header.
vs the recommended build: no enclosure, IEC inlet or high-flex chainflex cable; plain 22 AWG cable and one drag chain on Y only.

vs the recommended build: the CAD, Haas programs and printed parts are built around MGN15 rails, CL42T drivers and the Hitec servo. The V-wheel gantry plates, carriage and servo mount must be redesigned and re-verified, which is shop and design time not in the dollar total.
